findings.message: full_suite_acceptance_test declares a dependency on 'work_dir_validation_fixes', but no such task_id exists in the plan. The actual task is named '_work_dir_fixes'. This dangling reference will fail dependency resolution and is structurally equivalent to a broken DAG edge.

full_suite_acceptance_test declares a dependency on 'ast_merge_future_imports_fixes', which does not exist; the actual task is '_ast_merge_fixes'. Dangling dependency reference will block acceptance execution.

suggested_patch.rationale: Set count to match listed tests (3 unit + 1 integration).

findings.message: minimum_test_count is 10, but test_spec only enumerates 3 unit tests + 1 integration test (4 total). Property and regression test arrays are empty. This is an inflated benchmark claim — the floor cannot be met by the items the task itself declares.

suggested_patch.rationale: Acceptance task should not double-count tests already attributed to the source tasks (check_true_depth_fixes, janusmask_module_descriptor_fixes). It should only enumerate a single end-to-end run.

findings.message: The acceptance task lists 'test_depth_validator_integration', 'test_target_descriptor_integration' as its own unit tests — these are already enumerated in check_true_depth_fixes and janusmask_module_descriptor_fixes. Double-counting inflates aggregate test totals and misrepresents acceptance work.

suggested_patch.rationale: Drop integration_tests to honor the explicit non_goal.

findings.message: spec.non_goals explicitly states 'Do not write integration tests for check_true_depth' yet test_spec.integration_tests lists 'test_depth_validator_integration'. The plan internally contradicts itself; either the non-goal must be removed or the integration test entry dropped.

non_goals forbids integration tests for safe_under_project, but test_spec.integration_tests still lists 'test_safe_under_project_integration'. The minimum_test_count of 5 for an isinstance-guard one-liner (60 impl tokens) is also test-heavy — 2-3 focused unit tests would suffice.
non_goals: 'Do not write integration tests for descriptor.' contradicts test_spec.integration_tests containing 'test_target_descriptor_integration'. Same contradiction pattern as f-005/f-006.

non_goals forbids integration tests for _work_dir, yet test_spec.integration_tests lists 'test_work_dir_integration'. Additionally, 5 tests for two isinstance checks (60 impl tokens) is heavy — collapse to 2-3 unit tests.
non_goals: 'Do not write integration tests for _ast_merge' contradicts test_spec.integration_tests = ['test_ast_merge_integration']. Plan must be internally consistent.

suggested_patch.edge_case: Multi-hop cyclic lineage A -> B -> C -> A (cycle length > 1), distinct from self-cycle.

findings.message: edge_cases only enumerates a self-cycle (length 1). The visited-set guard must also be exercised against longer cycles (A->B->C->A) to prove it actually detects revisits across files, not just self-reference.

suggested_patch.edge_case: Output code contains NO __future__ imports (no-op path) — target body and main-guard index must be unchanged.

findings.message: edge_cases omits the negative case where the output has no __future__ imports at all. Without it, regressions that wrongly shift guard_idx or mutate target body in the empty case would be missed.

suggested_patch.edge_case: __future__ import already present in target but absent in output (dedupe path) should not reorder or duplicate.

findings.message: Deduplication is mentioned in functional_requirements but not pinned as an explicit edge case. Add coverage for: target-only existing __future__ import that should be preserved without reinsertion.

spec.interfaces still declares 'candidate: str' even though the acceptance criteria explicitly allow os.PathLike candidates. The signature in the spec contradicts the requirement and will mislead the implementer; update the type annotation in the interface.

suggested_patch.edge_case: seed_files is None (default) — must skip list unwrapping/validation and not raise.

findings.message: The interface advertises 'seed_files: list[str] | None = None' but edge_cases never specifies behavior when seed_files is None. The unwrap-and-validate path could erroneously raise TypeError on the default.

suggested_patch.rationale: 1.5x test:impl ratio is excessive for a single-line isinstance guard. Reduce test budget to 1:1 to match the trivial implementation.

findings.message: token_budget_ratio sets test_tokens at 1.5x implementation_tokens across every task uniformly, regardless of complexity. For the trivial isinstance guards (safe_under_project_fixes, _work_dir_fixes), this is disproportionate and incentivizes padding tests beyond what the change warrants.

verification_command is 'pytest -v test_target_generated.py' (project-root path) while other tasks point under 'tests/'. Inconsistent test-path convention risks the verification command not finding the test file.
